entities.summary:
Gwenwynwyn ab Owain Cyfeiliog, the last major ruler of mid Wales, played a crucial role in the region's politics before the Norman English invasion in the 13th century. As one of few native rulers to challenge Llywelyn the Great's dominance, Gwenwynwyn's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns and diplomatic maneuvers that ultimately failed to prevent the Norman conquest. Despite his significance in Welsh history, Gwenwynwyn's legacy has been overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporary, Llywelyn the Great.

Born around 1200, Gwenwynwyn's early life and ascension to power are shrouded in mystery, with some accounts suggesting he was the son of Owain Cyfeiliog, a powerful Welsh lord. He ruled mid Wales from around 1204 until his death in 1216, during which time he engaged in a series of battles with Llywelyn the Great's forces.

Gwenwynwyn's reign was also marked by a series of strategic alliances and diplomatic maneuvers aimed at securing his position and protecting his territory from the expanding Norman influence. However, these efforts ultimately proved unsuccessful, and he was defeated by Llywelyn the Great's forces in 1211.

Following his defeat, Gwenwynwyn went into hiding, and his whereabouts after 1211 are unknown. His legacy, however, continues to be felt in Welsh history, and he remains an important figure in the study of the medieval period in Wales.

Gwenwynwyn's significance extends beyond his own reign, as his failure to challenge Llywelyn the Great's dominance marked a turning point in the history of Wales, paving the way for the Norman conquest and the eventual absorption of Wales into the English crown.
